A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PLN-ICA/ARPLN-ICA research work. Their text, equations, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching retained content across pagination and figure renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original simulations of mixing recovery and original microbiome analyses, including regime inference, reconstruction, stability, and forecasting evaluations.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds original climate-data analyses, an additional forecasting comparator, and further simulation and microbiome results.

M1.justification: The generative model, structured variational approximation, CAVI/EM updates, neural parameterization, normalization, fixed effects, and forecasting procedure are retained. The climate application uses the existing method; P-rSLDS is an added comparator.

E1.justification: V2 adds the NOAA Storm Events application in Section 6 and Appendix I, analyzing monthly counts of 16 weather-hazard types across annual trajectories. This substantially extends actual evaluation coverage from simulations and microbiome dynamics to seasonal climate-event structure.

E2.justification: The microbiome forecasting comparison adds P-rSLDS, a Poisson log-link recurrent switching linear dynamical model, in Figure 6 and Appendix G.6. The existing homogeneous ARPLN-ICA, CLR-VAR(1), CLR-UWEDGEICA, CLR-PICARD, and gLV-L2 comparators remain; simulation comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 introduces leave-one-year-out climate evaluation over a reported 25 annual trajectories, using monthly aggregation, logsum offsets, and reconstruction metrics excluding Aitchison distance. Figure 3 adds training size n = 1. P-rSLDS uses two switching states and matched offsets. Existing simulation and microbiome protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix I.2 adds climate latent-dimension sensitivity and cross-fold component-stability analyses. Figure 3 extends the existing sample-size sensitivity analysis to one trajectory, and Section 5.3 quantifies the infection-associated component shift. Existing ablations, timing analyses, and microbiome sensitivity studies remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report ten differently initialized simulation fits, confidence intervals, and standard deviations across cross-validation folds. The added experiments extend these reporting practices without documenting changed repeat counts, seed procedures, or uncertainty-estimation methods for retained experiments.

E6.justification: V2 adds P-rSLDS forecasting scores, n = 1 recovery results, and the finding that microbiome component 4 accounts for 67% of the phase-related absolute mean shift. Climate results add seasonal patterns, reconstruction comparisons, and mixing similarity above 99.7%. Retained simulation recovery values of 74.6% and 84.5% are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 changes the stated domains in Lemmas A.1–A.2 from nonnegative intensity vectors excluding the zero vector to coordinatewise strictly positive intensities. This narrowly changes their boundary assumptions. The main identifiability results, proof arguments, and inference derivations are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion now claim recovery of seasonal regimes and meteorological patterns alongside microbial associations. The three principal contributions—count-specific ICA, mixing identifiability, and structured amortized inference—remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 adds meteorological interpretations and the climate reconstruction-versus-interpretability tradeoff. It attributes favorable Poisson deviance to both ARPLN-ICA and P-rSLDS and explicitly discusses nonlinear mixing as future work. The conclusion retains variational-inference and missing-data limitations but drops the explicit irregular-sampling caveat.

D1.justification: V2 explicitly advertises experiment-reproduction scripts alongside the previously linked implementation. It adds P-rSLDS implementation information using SSM, package-default settings, matched switching-state counts and offsets, plus NOAA dataset identifiers and climate processing details. Existing architecture, optimization, and hardware disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Poisson switching-model literature by Linderman, Zoltowski, and Glaser, alongside Qian and climate-related references. Section 2 and Appendix G.6 broaden positioning against existing Poisson dynamical models and distinguish ICA-compatible independent switching from P-rSLDS grouped switching. The central ICA positioning remains.

P1.justification: There are targeted revisions to the abstract, introduction, identifiability explanation, forecasting motivation, and conclusion, plus acknowledgements and new climate sections. The established narrative, method organization, and Appendices A–H are largely retained rather than extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: V2 expands Figures 3 and 6, adds the climate displays in Figures 7, 21, and 22, and introduces Table 1. Existing appendix figures are renumbered with their content retained. Local caption, legend, and pagination changes preserve the overall visual format.

improvement.justification: The climate case study, including held-out reconstruction and component-stability checks, broadens empirical support beyond v1's five-mouse application. Adding P-rSLDS makes the auxiliary forecasting comparison more informative and its Poisson-likelihood interpretation better supported. These provide useful corroboration; the central method and identifiability arguments remain intact, and the climate interpretations are still primarily qualitative.
